findings_qualitative.value: The circumstellar ejecta of VY CMa is composed of two distinct mass loss types: an extended, irregular, slower ejecta traced by SiO, SiS, SO, SO2, and 13CO, and localized fast outflows traced by H2S, NaCl, o-H2O, and continuum.

evidence.loc: History of two mass loss processes in VY CMa
evidence.quote: Two types of ejecta are clearly observed: extended, irregular, and vast ejecta surrounding the star that are carved by localized fast outflows.

The continuum emission (Fig. 1) presents relatively compact structures already identified in previous works (cite: Richards14; ogorman15; debeck15). These structures are also clearly traced by certain species such as H$_2$S or NaCl. On the other hand, the emission from SiO, SiS, SO or $^{13}$CO presents a more extended emission.

findings_qualitative.value: The fast localized outflows carve cavities and bubble-like shell structures into the previously ejected quiescent gas traced by SO and SiO.

evidence.quote: SiO and SO emission present clear signs of this carving, as the maps present no emission of these lines in the regions where the narrow outflows arise (see Fig 2).
This comparison shows that the outflows traced by H$_2$S and the shells probed by SO are related. In particular it suggests that the outflows are carving previous ejecta and forming cavities.

findings_qualitative.value: The fast outflows exhibit a flattened morphology orthogonal to their outflow axes with a width-to-height ratio of ~6.

evidence.quote: The extended outflows are well resolved and are found to have a flattened geometry (Fig. 9) in one of the directions orthogonal to the axis of the ejection when compared with pPNe bipolar outflows (cite: alcolea07). The ratio of width to height is $\sim\,6$.

findings_qualitative.value: The systemic velocity and position of VY CMa are better represented by V_LSR = 12 km s^-1 and the 232 GHz o-H2O maser peak rather than the previously assumed 22 km s^-1 and continuum peak.

evidence.quote: In addition, the fitting of the outflow connecting $VY$ and $C$ suggests the systemic velocity at $VY$ might not be 22 km s$^{-1}$ as previously thought (cite: Decin16; Richards14), but $V_{LSR}=$12 km s$^{-1}$.

Since the pumping mechanism of the maser is the IR emission from the central star, and the velocity of the peak corresponds to what we found to be compatible with the origin of the fast outflows, we propose that the position of this peak might correspond with the real position of the central star.

claims.hypothesis: Mass loss in VY CMa occurs via two distinct physical mechanisms: a steady, slower, ubiquitous wind and sporadic, fast, collimated outflows that carve the older ejecta.
claims.experiment: High angular resolution (~25-35 mas) ALMA imaging of multiple molecular tracers (SiO, SO, H2S, NaCl, o-H2O), PV diagram kinematic analysis, 3D reconstruction using Astructures, and spatial comparison of H2S jets with SO shell cavities.
claims.result: H2S and NaCl trace at least six fast outflows following a Hubble-like velocity law (v = 17 * r/0.1'' km s^-1, reaching 120-140 km s^-1), which spatially match cavities in the extended SiO and SO emission.
claims.finding: Two different mass loss processes operate in VY CMa: a slower wind likely driven by convective cells and dust radiation pressure, and energetic fast collimated outflows that carve the previously ejected slow wind.

evidence.quote: This coincidence of the jets and the holes clearly suggests the existence of two mass loss processes, and the carving of previously ejected material by the fast outflows.
The data presented show, for the first time, that mass loss within this phase can take place in two completely different ways.

claims.hypothesis: The fast collimated outflows in VY CMa are driven by radiation pressure on dust formed above long-lived cold starspots.
claims.experiment: Measure the velocity law of the A and C outflows from PV diagrams of NaCl and H2S and reconstruct their 3D cross-sectional geometry.
claims.result: The outflows follow a Hubble-like linear velocity field (V_exp proportional to r) reaching 120-140 km s^-1 and have a flattened geometry with a width-to-height ratio of ~6.
claims.finding: Radiation pressure on dust formed at circular cold spots is refuted as the driving mechanism because it cannot produce a Hubble-like velocity field or flattened outflows; instead, magnetically driven events like CMEs or a rotating active spot ('sprinkler') are required.

evidence.quote: Its important to note that this type of velocity field ($v\propto r$) cannot be created by the radiation pressure on dust grains, but a different mechanism might be the responsible for these ejections.

The presence of cold starspots alone could not generate the structures observed as they usually show a roughly circular shape, and the produced outflows are expected to have a similar similar cross section orthogonal to their outflow axes.
These fast winds could not be due to radiation pressure on dust formed at long-lived cold spots, as indicated by the velocity field, but were caused by other mechanisms.

claims.hypothesis: Coronal mass ejections (CMEs) or a rotating magnetically active spot (Sprinkler model) can explain the momentum and flattened morphology of the fast outflows.
claims.experiment: Calculate the linear momentum of clump C and the required magnetic field using CME scaling laws, and simulate 3D outflow shapes from a rotating star with active spots (Sprinkler model).
claims.result: Outflow C has momentum P = 9.30 x 10^38 g cm s^-1, requiring a ~5 kG magnetic field over 50 yr; the Sprinkler model reproduces the 3D H2S outflows with a nearly pole-on rotation axis (~95 deg) and t_e = 120/V_rot months.
claims.finding: Both CME-like magnetic eruptions and collimated ejections combined with stellar rotation are physically viable explanations for the flattened fast outflows.

evidence.quote: The magnetic field needed to provide the amount of momentum derived above is $\sim$5kG.

In summary, the structure, the magnetic field strength, and the position angle (P.A.) of the different jets, and also the Hubble-like velocity field therefore seem compatible with outflows of magnetic origin, for example coronal mass ejections.
This is a simple approximation that confirms that the molecular emission observed for the fast outflows can be formed in this manner.

claims.hypothesis: The true stellar position and systemic velocity of VY CMa correspond to the 232 GHz o-H2O maser peak at V_LSR = 12 km s^-1 rather than the continuum peak and V_LSR = 22 km s^-1.
claims.experiment: Fit the Hubble velocity field of outflow C to find its origin velocity, map the high-excitation o-H2O v2=1 maser, and trace back the 3D axes of the six H2S and NaCl outflows to compare V_LSR = 12 km s^-1 vs 22 km s^-1.
claims.result: The o-H2O maser peaks intensely at ~12 km s^-1 at R.A. 07h22m58s.327 Dec. -25d46m03s.06, and the 3D outflow axes converge on V_LSR = 12 km s^-1.
claims.finding: V_LSR = 12 km s^-1 and the o-H2O maser peak better represent the systemic velocity and position of the central star than the continuum peak and mean profile velocity (22 km s^-1).

evidence.quote: Since the pumping mechanism of the maser is the IR emission from the central star, and the velocity of the peak corresponds to what we found to be compatible with the origin of the fast outflows, we propose that the position of this peak might correspond with the real position of the central star.

evidence.loc: Position and systemic velocity of the star
evidence.quote: In the 3D videos labeled “lines” we plotted the axis and the two positions for the central source as a filled star corresponding to a $V_\mathrm{LSR} = 12\mbox{km~s$^{-1}$}$ and a filled circle for $V_\mathrm{LSR} = 22\mbox{km~s$^{-1}$}$. It can be seen that the former value seems more compatible with the ejections.

why_this_data.value: High angular resolution (~25-35 mas) ALMA observations of molecular emission provide spatio-kinematical information in the inner ejecta to disentangle mass ejection mechanisms in VY CMa.

evidence.quote: In particular, the molecular emission from these ejecta provides spatio-kinematical information which allows us to reconstruct the events generating the ejection.
In order to study the characteristics of the ejecta, and the processes driving these mass ejections we obtained ALMA molecular maps of VY CMa with an angular resolution of $\sim 25-35$ mas

why_this_method.value: 3D reconstruction using the expansion velocity law from PV diagrams transforms the velocity axis into spatial depth, enabling identification of multiple overlapping outflows and cavities in a complex circumstellar structure.

evidence.quote: Due to the complex structure of the ejecta we generated 3D structures imposing the expansion velocity field obtained from the PV diagrams using the `Astructures code`.
Assuming a given velocity field, this dimension can be transformed into a space dimension, allowing us to reconstruct a 3D spatial structure.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Radiation pressure on dust grains formed at circular cold starspots rejected as the driver of the fast collimated outflows because it cannot produce a Hubble-like velocity law or a flattened cross-section.

evidence.quote: Its important to note that this type of velocity field ($v\propto r$) cannot be created by the radiation pressure on dust grains, but a different mechanism might be the responsible for these ejections.

The presence of cold starspots alone could not generate the structures observed as they usually show a roughly circular shape, and the produced outflows are expected to have a similar similar cross section orthogonal to their outflow axes.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Cold-spot groupings considered less likely than helmet streamers / CMEs to produce the observed flattened outflow morphology.

evidence.quote: On the other hand, a cold-spot grouping is unlikely to generate the shape of the ejections presented here, which in fact resembles the structure of the helmet streamers (cite: Glukhov_1997) and the final stages of the CMEs (cite: Gibson_1998).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Higher exponential orders for the expansion velocity law were tested and rejected as the cause of the outflow flatness because flatness is maintained across velocity laws.

evidence.quote: In addition, we have modified the velocity law from constant expansion to higher exponential orders, and this flatness is maintained.

limitations_admitted.value: Extended homogeneous emission on scales larger than ~0.4 arcsec (maximum recoverable scale 0.36 arcsec) is partially filtered out by the interferometer.

evidence.quote: Baselines ranged from 41m to 16km, providing an angular resolution $\sim 0\mbox{\rlap{.}$''$}025$ and with maximum recoverable scale for the most extended emission of $0\mbox{\rlap{.}$''$}36$.
The extended emission is partially filtered out.
The flux filtering affects structures with scales larger than $\sim$0$''$4.

limitations_admitted.value: Some detected molecular lines are too weak to obtain usable maps.

evidence.quote: Some of these lines were detected, but are too weak to obtain a usable map.

limitations_admitted.value: There is a twofold degeneracy between jet inclination (theta) and the velocity constant (V_0) when fitting PV diagrams.

evidence.quote: In order to fit the velocity field of these outflows, we took into account a twofold degeneracy. There is a series of pairs of values of the jet inclination with respect to the plane of the sky ($\theta$) and the value of the velocity constant ($V_0$), which would fit the velocity field of the outflow.

limitations_admitted.value: Cannot completely rule out that the northern VY-A jet arises from VY at V_LSR = 26 km s^-1 rather than 12 km s^-1.

evidence.quote: Nevertheless, the possibility of the $VY$–$A$ jet arising from $VY$ at 26 km s$^{-1}$ cannot be completely ruled out, and future observations will shed light on this fact.

limitations_admitted.value: Cannot determine whether the bullet-like structure of the two rear outflows is real or due to low S/N.

evidence.quote: For the last two outflows only bullet-like structures are visible. We cannot determine if the bullet-like structure of these outflows is real or due to a lack of S/N in the obtained maps.

limitations_admitted.value: Complex velocity field of SO prevents a 3D reconstruction of the SO emission.

evidence.quote: As mentioned, the velocity field of SO is particularly complex, and different from that observed for the fast outflows. This prevented a 3D reconstruction and a direct comparison of the structures traced by SO and H$_2$S.

limitations_admitted.value: Angular resolution (~30 x 20 mas) is not high enough to resolve the structure of the inner o-H2O outflows.

evidence.quote: This emission is constrained to the innermost regions of the envelope around the star and is barely resolved (half power beam width, HPBW, $\sim 30 \times 20$mas).
The resolution is not high enough to resolve the structure of the outflows.

referee_caveats_inferred: The 3D reconstruction relies on assuming the same single velocity gradient (17 km/s per 0.1 arcsec, derived from clump C assuming a 15 deg inclination) for all outflows, so any variation in inclination or velocity constant among the other outflows directly distorts their reconstructed 3D line-of-sight depths and shapes.
The Sprinkler model and the CME momentum model are heuristic/analytical approximations rather than self-consistent magnetohydrodynamic or radiative transfer simulations.
Lack of short-spacing data filters out >0.36 arcsec scales, which could affect the apparent morphology of the cavities in the extended SiO and SO emission.

code_released.value: Astructures code publicly available on GitHub at https://github.com/GQuintanaL/Astructures

evidence.quote: `https://github.com/GQuintanaL/Astructures`

missing_for_reproduction: Exact self-calibration parameters (solution intervals, number of phase-only vs amplitude+phase rounds, S/N thresholds)
Exact Briggs robust value and SDI cleaning stopping criteria/masking
Exact channel ranges used for uv continuum subtraction in each spectral window
Exact position angles and widths of the PV diagram slices for VY-C and VY-A
Source code or exact mathematical equations for the Sprinkler kinematic model
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~20-50 GB (single 1.3h execution block in Cycle 5 with 51 antennas on long baselines up to 16 km and four 1.875 GHz spectral windows at ~1.3 km/s resolution)
reproducibility.score_reason: The ALMA project code is stated, the 3D reconstruction tool (Astructures) is released on GitHub, and the kinematic assumptions and Sprinkler model parameters are tabulated, but low-level imaging/self-calibration parameters, PV slice position angles, and the Sprinkler model script are not specified.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public Cycle 5 ALMA dataset (2017.1.00558.S) with clear quantitative findings (line identifications, PV velocity gradient, systemic velocity V_LSR = 12 km/s, maser and continuum peak positions, and 3D outflow geometry) and an open-source 3D reconstruction tool.

methods_papers.why: SDI cleaning method used for image synthesis
MADEX spectroscopic database/tool used to identify molecular species
Scaling relation for magnetic momentum transfer in CMEs
